```{r}
# Q6: Exhaustive Search Implementation

# Generate a random number between 1 and 50
User_Input <- sample(1:50, 1) # This simulates the user selecting a number

# We can manually set the input for testing the 'TRUE' condition:
# User_Input <- 20

cat("Chosen number:", User_Input, "\n")

if (User_Input < 1 || User_Input > 50) {
  # If the number is beyond the range
  print("The number selected is beyond the range of 1 to 50")
} else if (User_Input == 20) {
  # If number 20 is inputted
  print("TRUE")
} else {
  # Otherwise, display the input number
  print(User_Input)
}
```

```{r}
# Q7: Minimum Number of Bills Function
# Available bills: 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000

calculate_min_bills <- function(price) {
  # Bills are listed from largest to smallest for greedy approach
  bills <- c(1000, 500, 200, 100, 50)
  num_bills <- 0
  remaining_price <- price

  for (bill in bills) {
    if (remaining_price >= bill) {
      # Calculate how many of the current bill are needed
      count <- floor(remaining_price / bill)
      num_bills <- num_bills + count
      # Update the remaining amount
      remaining_price <- remaining_price - (count * bill)
    }
  }

  cat("Price of snack:", price, "pesos\n")
  return(num_bills)
}

# Test cases:
# Random price divisible by 50 between 100 and 1500
random_price <- sample(seq(100, 1500, by = 50), 1)
min_bills_needed <- calculate_min_bills(random_price)
cat("Minimum number of bills needed to purchase a snack:", min_bills_needed)
```

```{r}
# Q8a: Create data frame from table
Name <- c("Annie", "Thea", "Steve", "Hanna")
Grade1 <- c(85, 65, 75, 95)
Grade2 <- c(65, 75, 55, 75)
Grade3 <- c(85, 90, 80, 100)
Grade4 <- c(100, 90, 85, 90)

df_grades <- data.frame(Name, Grade1, Grade2, Grade3, Grade4)
print("Student Grades Data Frame:")
df_grades
```

```{r}
# Q8b: Average score over 90 (without mean function)

for (i in 1:nrow(df_grades)) {
  # Calculate sum and count manually
  total_score <- df_grades[i, "Grade1"] + df_grades[i, "Grade2"] + df_grades[i, "Grade3"] + df_grades[i, "Grade4"]
  grade_count <- 4 # Number of grades is fixed at 4
  average <- total_score / grade_count

  # Check condition
  if (average > 90) {
    cat(df_grades[i, "Name"], "'s average grade this semester is ", average, ".\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Q8c: Output tests where average score was less than 80 (without mean function)

# Extract only the grade columns
grades_only <- df_grades[, 2:5] # Grade1 to Grade4

for (j in 1:ncol(grades_only)) {
  # Calculate column sum and column count manually
  col_sum <- sum(grades_only[, j])
  col_count <- nrow(grades_only)
  test_average <- col_sum / col_count

  # Check condition
  if (test_average < 80) {
    # Test column index j corresponds to the nth test (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th)
    cat("The ", j, "th test was difficult.\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Q8d: Students whose highest score exceeds 90 (without max function)

for (i in 1:nrow(df_grades)) {
  student_grades <- as.numeric(df_grades[i, 2:5]) # Get the four grades

  # Check if any grade is greater than 90.
  # We use the 'any' function to check for the condition across the vector.
  if (any(student_grades > 90)) {
    # Manually find the maximum (instead of using max())
    highest_grade <- -Inf # Initialize with negative infinity
    for (grade in student_grades) {
      if (grade > highest_grade) {
        highest_grade <- grade
      }
    }
    cat(df_grades[i, "Name"], "'s highest grade this semester is ", highest_grade, ".\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```
